items.zh: 四無量心 · 修慈證慈

zh: 第四、正明修證。約四無量心，即自有四：一、修慈證慈；二、修悲證悲；三、修喜證喜：四、修捨證捨。第一、明修慈證慈者，即開為二：第一、正明修習方法，此如佛處處經中說：「有比丘以慈相應心，無恚無恨，無怨無惱，廣大無量，善修習。」云何名以慈相應心？如《釋論》說：「若念十方眾生令得樂時，心數法中生法，名為慈。」善是相應，欲入禪定，當先作誓願：「一切眾生悉受快樂，我於定中悉得見受、想、行、識。」是名心數法。諸身業、口業及心不相應諸行是法和合，皆名為慈。是法皆以慈為主，故慈得名。譬如一切心數法皆是後世因緣，而但思得名，於作業中，思最有力故，是名慈相應相。
en: Fourth, directly clarifying cultivation and realization. With reference to the four immeasurable minds, this itself has four parts: cultivating and realizing loving-kindness; cultivating and realizing compassion; cultivating and realizing sympathetic joy; and cultivating and realizing equanimity.

First, clarifying the cultivation and realization of loving-kindness: this opens into two parts. First, directly clarifying the method of cultivation: this is exactly as the Buddha says throughout the sūtras, everywhere: "There is a monk who, with a mind corresponding to loving-kindness, free of anger, free of resentment, free of enmity, free of vexation, vast and immeasurable, cultivates it well." What is meant by "a mind corresponding to loving-kindness"? As the Exegetical Treatise says: "Whenever one holds the ten directions' sentient beings in mind, wishing them to attain happiness, the dharma that arises within the mental factors is what is named loving-kindness." Being properly corresponding, one wishing to enter dhyāna-concentration should first make this vow: "May all sentient beings receive complete happiness — may I, within concentration, come to see this in every case." Sensation, perception, formation, and consciousness corresponding with it — these are what are named the mental-factor dharmas. Every bodily action, verbal action, and every activity not directly corresponding with the mind, this dharma taken together as a whole, is named loving-kindness. Since this dharma, in every case, takes loving-kindness as its ruling factor, it receives the name "loving-kindness" accordingly. It is like every mental factor being, in its own right, a cause and condition for a future life, and yet receiving its name simply from intention alone, since, among the various karmic actions, intention is the most powerful of all — this is the mark of a mind corresponding to loving-kindness.

zh: 復次，行者初修時，用念清淨心，取外所愛親人受樂之相，若父母兄弟隨取一最愛者，一心緣之。若有異念，攝之令還，令於心想的的分明，見於親人受樂之相。其心愛念，乃至中人、怨人，餘五道亦如是。復次，行者如是修時，若見種種善惡境界及發諸禪中事，悉不得取，但一心觀於親人得樂之相，心心相續。是則略說修慈方法。
en: Furthermore: the practitioner, at the outset of cultivation, uses a mind of pure mindfulness to take up the mark of an outwardly loved one's own happiness — if it is a parent or a sibling, taking up whichever one is most beloved, fixing the mind single-mindedly upon them. Should some other thought arise, one gathers the mind back in, making the mental image entirely clear and distinct, seeing the mark of this loved one's own happiness. This loving regard of mind is then extended, in turn, to neutral persons and even to enemies, and to the remaining five realms as well, following the same pattern. Furthermore: the practitioner, cultivating in this way, should, even upon seeing various wholesome or unwholesome states, or matters arising from within the various dhyānas, take up none of them at all — simply contemplating, single-mindedly, the mark of the loved one's own happiness, mind following mind in unbroken continuity. This, in brief, describes the method for cultivating loving-kindness.

zh: 第二、明慈定發相。行者禪定智慧、福德善根力清淨故，如是一心慈念眾生時，三昧即發。三昧力故，即於定心中見所愛親人受於快樂之相，身心悅豫，顏色和適，了了分明。如是見親人得樂已，次見中人乃至怨人亦復如是。於定心中見一人，次見於十人、千人、萬億、一聚落、一國土、一閻浮提、一四天下，乃至十方世界一切眾生，悉皆受樂。行者於定中見外人受樂，而內定轉深，與外相應，湛然無動，是名慈相應心。即是相應受、想、行、識、陰、入、界等法，如前說。問曰：慈相應定見眾生時，為當如上說，從一至十漸漸而見，為當一時併見？答曰：行者根有漸、頓、不定。
en: Second, clarifying the mark of the loving-kindness concentration's own arising. The practitioner, through the pure power of dhyāna-concentration, wisdom, merit, and wholesome roots, holding sentient beings single-mindedly in loving-kindness in this way, samādhi is thereby brought forth. Through the power of this samādhi, one sees, within the concentrated mind, the mark of the loved one's own happiness, body and mind delighted, countenance at ease, entirely clear and distinct. Having seen the loved one attain happiness in this way, one next sees the same for a neutral person, and then even for an enemy as well. Within the concentrated mind, one sees a single person; then one sees ten people, a thousand, myriads upon myriads; a single village; a single country; a single Jambudvīpa; a single set of the four continents; and, further still, every sentient being throughout the worlds of the ten directions, all alike receiving happiness.

The practitioner, seeing others receiving happiness within concentration, while the inward concentration itself grows ever deeper, corresponding with what is seen without, deep and unmoving — this is named the mind corresponding with loving-kindness. This is precisely the corresponding dharma of sensation, perception, formation, and consciousness, the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements, exactly as already described above. Question: within the concentration corresponding with loving-kindness, when sentient beings are seen, is it exactly as described above, seen gradually, one at a time up through ten, or are they all seen together, all at once? Answer: practitioners' own faculties differ — gradual, sudden, or unfixed.

zh: 一種慈相應心者，慈名心數法，能除心中憒濁，所謂瞋、恨、慳、貪煩惱。譬如淨水明珠置濁水中，水即澄清。無恚無恨，無怨無惱者，於眾生中，若有因緣，若無因緣，初生名為瞋；瞋增長籌量，持著心中而未決了，是名為恨，亦名為怨；若心已定，無所畏忌，欲損於他，是名為惱。以慈心力除、捨、離此三事，是名無瞋無恨，無怨無惱。此無瞋無恨，無怨無惱，以是讚歎慈心功德。
en: As for the single mind corresponding with loving-kindness: loving-kindness, being a mental factor, is able to remove the mind's own turbidity — namely, the afflictions of anger, resentment, stinginess, and craving. It is like a clear-water pearl placed into turbid water: the water is thereby made clear at once. As for being free of anger, free of resentment, free of enmity, and free of vexation: toward sentient beings, whether for some cause or condition, or for none at all, the initial arising of ill will is named anger; anger, growing and deliberating further, held fixed within the mind without yet being resolved, is named resentment, also called enmity; and, once the mind has become fixed on it, with no fear or restraint left, wishing to harm the other, this is named vexation. Through the power of loving-kindness, removing, relinquishing, and leaving behind these three matters is what is named being free of anger, free of resentment, free of enmity, and free of vexation. These qualities are given here in praise of loving-kindness's own merit.

zh: 廣大無量者，一心分別，有二種名：如慈相緣見一方為廣，四方為大，緣四維及上下為無量。復次，破瞋恨心名為廣，破怨心名為大，破惱心名為無量。慈緣親人為廣，慈緣中人為大，慈緣怨人得福多，故名無量。復次，為狹緣故，名為廣。為小緣故，名為大。為有量緣，故名無量。善修者，是慈心牢固。初得慈，不名為善修；非但愛念眾生中，非但好眾生中，非但益一眾生中，非但一方眾生中，名為善修。行者於上親、中親、下親、上中人、中中人、下中人、下怨、中怨、上怨，是九種人中，愛憎正等無異，乃至愛念五道眾生中，以一慈心視之如父如母，如兄弟、子姪、知識，常求好事，欲令利益安樂，如是之心遍滿十方，是名善修。復次，若但與眾生欲界樂，不名善修；但與初禪樂，不名善修；但與二禪樂，不名善修。若能具足與欲界樂，乃至三、四禪樂，是名善修。
en: As for "vast and immeasurable": distinguished single-mindedly, this carries two kinds of name. In terms of loving-kindness's own object: taking a single direction as its object is "vast"; taking all four directions is "great"; and taking the four intermediate directions together with above and below is "immeasurable." Furthermore: breaking through anger and resentment is named "vast"; breaking through enmity is named "great"; and breaking through vexation is named "immeasurable." Loving-kindness taking a loved one as its object is "vast"; taking a neutral person as its object is "great"; and taking an enemy as its object, gaining the greater merit thereby, is named "immeasurable." Furthermore: in contrast to a narrow object, it is named "vast"; in contrast to a small object, it is named "great"; and in contrast to a limited object, it is named "immeasurable."

As for "cultivated well": this means loving-kindness of mind made secure and firm. Merely first attaining loving-kindness is not yet named cultivating it well; loving-kindness confined only to loving certain sentient beings, only to those one already likes, only to benefiting a single sentient being, or only to sentient beings in a single direction, cannot be named cultivating it well either. The practitioner, among these nine kinds of person — the highest, middle, and lowest grade of loved one; the highest, middle, and lowest grade of neutral person; and the lowest, middle, and highest grade of enemy — holds love and aversion exactly equal, with no distinction at all between them, extending this loving regard even to sentient beings across all five realms, viewing each with this same single mind of loving-kindness as though they were one's own father, one's own mother, one's own sibling, child, nephew or niece, or close friend, constantly seeking what is good for them, wishing to bring them benefit and peace — such a mind as this, pervading all ten directions completely, is what is named cultivating it well. Furthermore: bestowing upon sentient beings only the happiness of the desire realm cannot be named cultivating it well; bestowing only the happiness of the first dhyāna cannot be named cultivating it well; bestowing only the happiness of the second dhyāna cannot be named cultivating it well either. Only if one is able to bestow, in full completeness, the happiness of the desire realm all the way through the happiness of the third and fourth dhyānas, is this named cultivating it well.

zh: 如是慈心，名眾生緣。或在凡夫人行處，或有學人未漏盡者亦行此悲為調心，得大福德，入無漏故。法緣者，諸漏盡阿羅漢、辟支佛、諸佛，是諸聖人破吾我相，滅一異相故，但觀從因緣相續生。以慈念眾生時，從和合因緣相續，但空五陰即是眾生，念是五陰。此慈念眾生不知是法空，眾生常一心欲得樂，聖人愍之，令隨意得樂，為世俗法故，名為法緣。無緣者，是慈但諸佛有。何以故？諸佛不住有為、無為性中，不依上、下、過去、未來、現在，知諸因緣為不實，顛倒虛誑，故心無所緣。佛以眾生不知是諸法實相，往來五道，心著諸法，而分別取捨，以是諸法實相智慧令眾生得之，是為無緣。譬如給濟貧人，或與財物、金銀、寶物，或與如意神珠。眾生緣、法緣、無緣亦復如是。此義如《摩訶衍》中廣說。
en: Loving-kindness of this kind is named loving-kindness that takes sentient beings as its object. This may be practiced by an ordinary person, or by a trainee who has not yet exhausted the contaminants, cultivating this compassion in order to regulate the mind, gaining great merit, and thereby entering the uncontaminated.

As for loving-kindness that takes dharma as its object: arhats who have exhausted every contaminant, pratyekabuddhas, and buddhas — these noble ones, having broken through the mark of self, and extinguished the mark of sameness and difference, contemplate only the continuous arising of things through causes and conditions. When holding sentient beings in loving-kindness, they see only the continuity of causes and conditions combining together — the empty five aggregates are themselves precisely what "sentient being" refers to, and it is these five aggregates that are held in mind. Sentient beings, not knowing that this dharma is empty, constantly wish single-mindedly to attain happiness; the noble ones, taking pity on them, allow them to attain happiness according to their own wish, for the sake of this same conventional dharma — hence this is named loving-kindness that takes dharma as its object.

As for objectless loving-kindness: this loving-kindness belongs only to the buddhas. Why is this? The buddhas do not dwell within the nature of either the conditioned or the unconditioned, do not rely upon high or low, past, future, or present, and know that all causes and conditions are unreal, inverted and illusory — hence the mind has nothing at all that it takes as an object. The Buddha, because sentient beings do not know the true mark of all dharmas, and so come and go through the five realms, the mind clinging to dharmas, discriminating, taking up and rejecting — through this very wisdom of the true mark of all dharmas, causes sentient beings to attain it as well: this is objectless loving-kindness. It is like giving relief to the poor: one might give them wealth and goods, gold, silver, and jewels; or one might give them a wish-fulfilling spirit-jewel instead. Loving-kindness that takes sentient beings as its object, loving-kindness that takes dharma as its object, and objectless loving-kindness are exactly the same in this respect. This sense is given at length within the Mahāyāna treatise.

zh: 復次，眾生緣慈，但見受果報樂相；法緣慈，則見受諸法門及涅槃樂相；無緣慈，則見一切同是佛性常樂平等相。復次，眾生緣慈，則在根本禪中；法緣慈，多在特勝、通明、背捨諸無漏禪中；無緣慈，多是首楞嚴、法華三昧及九種禪中。
en: Furthermore: loving-kindness that takes sentient beings as its object sees only the mark of happiness received as a karmic result; loving-kindness that takes dharma as its object sees the mark of happiness received through the various dharma-gates and nirvāṇa itself; and objectless loving-kindness sees the mark that all things alike share the same buddha-nature, permanent, blissful, and equal. Furthermore: loving-kindness that takes sentient beings as its object belongs to the root dhyānas; loving-kindness that takes dharma as its object belongs, for the most part, to the special-excellences, the thorough-and-bright contemplation, the liberations, and the other uncontaminated dhyānas; and objectless loving-kindness belongs, for the most part, to the Śūraṅgama, the Lotus samādhi, and the nine kinds of dhyāna.

The three-tier structure here (sentient-being-object, dharma-object, objectless) directly parallels fascicle 3's own three-tier scheme for loving-kindness within the internal expedient means' wholesome-root marks — confirmation that this is a stable structure the treatise applies consistently wherever loving-kindness is analyzed in depth, not a one-off scheme. The wish-fulfilling-jewel-versus-ordinary-wealth simile makes a point worth carrying forward: all three levels are genuinely loving-kindness, differing only in the depth of what they're actually able to give — conventional happiness, versus the dharma-gates themselves, versus the very wisdom that dissolves the distinction between giver and given. The fire-by-friction simile in the compassion section that follows addresses a real objection: how can contemplating all beings as "receiving happiness" be anything but self-deception given how much of the world plainly suffers? The treatise's answer has two layers: this is an understanding deliberately brought to mind in contemplation and widened step by step, like a fire grown from soft kindling, not a factual claim about anyone's present circumstances; and it is not inverted, because suffering and happiness are themselves never fixed for any being across the five realms.

quiz.q: Which sūtra passage describes cultivating loving-kindness?
options: passing beyond every mark of form
the four emptinesses extinguish the path of form
a monk with a mind corresponding to loving-kindness, free of anger, resentment, enmity, and vexation, vast and immeasurable, cultivates it well
five factors as cause, silence as substance
quiz.why: The Buddha says throughout the sūtras that a monk with a mind corresponding to loving-kindness, free of anger and the rest, vast and immeasurable, cultivates it well. The other passages belong to the formless concentrations.

quiz.q: How does the Exegetical Treatise define loving-kindness?
options: when one holds beings of the ten directions in mind wishing them happiness, the dharma arising among the mental factors is loving-kindness
quiz.why: Loving-kindness is the dharma arising among the mental factors when one wishes beings of the ten directions to be happy. Pity on seeing suffering is compassion.

quiz.q: Why are bodily, verbal, and other activities together all called loving-kindness, and what comparison is given?
options: body, speech, and mind are one
loving-kindness rules them, as all mental factors are causes for future lives yet are named only by intention, the most powerful
quiz.why: Since loving-kindness rules them all, they take its name, just as all mental factors cause future lives but the name goes to intention, the most powerful in karmic action.

quiz.q: At the outset of cultivating loving-kindness, what mark does the practitioner take up?
options: the happiness of an outwardly loved one, such as the most beloved parent or sibling
quiz.why: With a mind of pure mindfulness, one takes up the happiness of a loved one, such as the most beloved parent or sibling, then extends to neutral persons, enemies, and the five realms.

quiz.q: While cultivating loving-kindness, if various wholesome or unwholesome states or dhyāna phenomena arise, what should one do?
options: take up none of them, simply contemplating the loved one's happiness in unbroken continuity
keep the wholesome, drop the unwholesome
quiz.why: One takes up none of them, wholesome ones included, and simply contemplates the loved one's happiness, mind following mind.

quiz.q: When the concentration of loving-kindness arises, in what order are beings seen receiving happiness?
options: first a loved one, then neutral persons and enemies; from one person to ten, a country, Jambudvīpa, up to all beings of the ten directions
the ten directions first, narrowing to one
quiz.why: Having seen the loved one happy, one sees neutral persons and enemies; one person, then ten, a thousand, a village, a country, Jambudvīpa, the four continents, up to all beings of the ten directions.

quiz.q: In the concentration of loving-kindness, are beings seen gradually or all at once?
options: practitioners' faculties differ: gradual, sudden, or unfixed
only buddhas see all at once
quiz.why: The answer is that practitioners' faculties differ, gradual, sudden, or unfixed, so no single pattern holds.

quiz.q: Loving-kindness removes the mind's turbidity. What simile illustrates it?
options: a clear-water pearl placed in turbid water makes it clear at once
an inchworm at the tip of a branch
quiz.why: As a mental factor, loving-kindness removes anger, resentment, stinginess, and craving, like a clear-water pearl clearing turbid water.

quiz.q: How does the text distinguish anger, resentment (enmity), and vexation?
options: by the object: loved, neutral, enemy
the first arising is anger; growing and held unresolved is resentment or enmity; fixed, fearless, and wishing harm is vexation
quiz.why: Ill will at first arising is anger; grown and held unresolved it is resentment, also enmity; once fixed and fearless, wishing to harm, it is vexation.

quiz.q: What, according to the text, is the function of "free of anger, resentment, enmity, and vexation"?
options: it praises the merit of loving-kindness
it lists four factors of the concentration
it requires these to be severed beforehand
quiz.why: Removing these through the power of loving-kindness is what the phrase means, and it is given in praise of loving-kindness's merit; it is a result, not a precondition.

quiz.q: In terms of directions, what do "vast," "great," and "immeasurable" refer to?
options: one direction is vast, four directions great, the intermediate directions with above and below immeasurable
quiz.why: One direction is "vast," the four directions "great," and the intermediate directions with above and below "immeasurable." Other pairings follow.

quiz.q: In terms of persons, why is loving-kindness toward an enemy called "immeasurable"?
options: because directing it to an enemy gains greater merit
quiz.why: Toward a loved one it is "vast," toward a neutral person "great," and toward an enemy, gaining greater merit, "immeasurable."

quiz.q: Which of the following does the text call "cultivating it well"?
options: holding love and aversion equal among the nine kinds of person and viewing all beings as parents, pervading the ten directions
quiz.why: Cultivating well means loving-kindness made firm. First attaining it, or loving only some beings or one direction, does not count; holding all nine kinds of person equally and pervading the ten directions does.

quiz.q: In terms of the happiness bestowed, what counts as cultivating it well?
options: bestowing in full the happiness of the desire realm through the third and fourth dhyānas
quiz.why: Giving only the happiness of the desire realm, or of the first or second dhyāna, is not cultivating well; giving all of it through the third and fourth dhyānas is.

quiz.q: Who practices loving-kindness that takes sentient beings as its object?
options: ordinary people, or trainees who have not exhausted the contaminants
quiz.why: Loving-kindness toward beings is practiced by ordinary people or by trainees not yet free of contaminants. Arhats and the like practice it with dharma as object; only buddhas have the objectless kind.

quiz.q: What do the noble ones who practice loving-kindness with dharma as object see when holding beings in mind?
options: only the continuity of combining causes and conditions; the empty five aggregates are what "sentient being" means
quiz.why: Having broken the mark of self, they see only the continuity of causes; the empty five aggregates are themselves what "sentient being" refers to. Seeing buddha-nature belongs to objectless loving-kindness.

quiz.q: Why does objectless loving-kindness belong only to the buddhas?
options: buddhas abide only in the fourth dhyāna
buddhas take only nirvāṇa as object
buddhas no longer care for beings
buddhas dwell in neither the conditioned nor the unconditioned, rely on no time, and know all conditions unreal, so the mind has no object
quiz.why: The buddhas dwell in neither the conditioned nor the unconditioned and know all causes and conditions to be unreal, so the mind has no object; they still bring beings the wisdom of the true mark.

quiz.q: In the simile of giving relief to the poor, what does giving a wish-fulfilling jewel correspond to?
options: objectless loving-kindness, which gives beings the wisdom of the true mark
quiz.why: Giving goods and gold corresponds to the lesser kinds; giving the wish-fulfilling jewel corresponds to objectless loving-kindness, which lets beings attain the wisdom of the true mark themselves.

quiz.q: In which kinds of dhyāna is each of the three kinds of loving-kindness mostly found?
options: beings: root dhyānas; dharma: special-excellences, thorough-and-bright, liberations; objectless: Śūraṅgama, Lotus samādhi, nine kinds of dhyāna
quiz.why: Beings-object loving-kindness belongs to the root dhyānas; dharma-object mostly to the special-excellences, thorough-and-bright, and liberations; objectless mostly to the Śūraṅgama, Lotus samādhi, and nine kinds of dhyāna.
